title: Table of Squares
code:
# Table of Squares Program

numbers_to_print = 10
i = 1

while i <= numbers_to_print:
    square = i * i
    print(i, "squared =", square)
    i += 1

print("Done!")

lines.explanation: Setting up the numbers to printed as '10'. This means that squares of numbers from 1 to 10 will be printed in the program
Initializing the loop condition variable to '1'
Initializing the 'while' loop with the condition to iterate until 'i' is less than or equal to 'numbers_to_print' (that means iterate till 'i' is less than or equal to 10)
This statement simply squares the number by multiplying the number with itself
This statement prints out the square of the number
Incrementing the value of 'i'. This is an important step in the 'while' loop. If the value of 'i' is not incremented, the 'while' loop will execute infinitely
When the condition is not True ('i' is greater than 'numbers_to_print'), it will exit the while loop and print the string 'Done!' to inform the user that the program is terminated.
